rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it overstates confidence in features not clearly visible in this single image, especially calling it a hatching blastocyst and describing a well-defined blastocoel/zona thinning when the image appears somewhat collapsed/out of focus and does not clearly show herniation.
Thoroughly integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve, prior IVF outcomes, male factor diagnosis, partner age, and untested embryo status into prognosis and counseling.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimates tied to morphology and patient factors; only minor overconfidence from morphology-image concordance limits a perfect score.

Recommendations are broadly aligned with IVF practice guidelines, including SET for a high-quality day-5 blastocyst and cautious discussion of PGT-A; minor issues include some imprecise wording around implantation/live birth probabilities and luteal support context.

Provides clear next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, including SET, uterine reassessment, optional PGT-A discussion, sperm DNA fragmentation consideration, and weight optimization; useful though not highly protocol-specific.
